Question: Convex quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has \(AB = 9\) and \(CD = 12.\) Diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(E,\) \(AC = 14,\) and \(\triangle AED\) and \(\triangle BEC\) have equal areas. What is \(AE?\)
Solution:
Method 1: Compare areas using shared heights

The equal areas can reveal side ratios if we compare both triangles with \(\triangle AEB\). Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of \(\triangle XYZ\). Convexity places \(E\) strictly inside both diagonals, so all the segment lengths and triangle areas used below are positive.

Triangles \(AED\) and \(AEB\) have bases on \(BD\) and share the same height from \(A\). Similarly, triangles \(BEC\) and \(AEB\) have bases on \(AC\) and share the same height from \(B\). Consequently,
\[
\frac{[AED]}{[AEB]}=\frac{ED}{EB},
\qquad
\frac{[BEC]}{[AEB]}=\frac{EC}{EA}.
\]
Since \([AED]=[BEC]\), these ratios are equal. Rearranging gives
\[
\frac{EA}{EC}=\frac{EB}{ED}.
\]
Also, \(\angle AEB=\angle CED\) because they are vertical angles. Thus \(\triangle AEB\) and \(\triangle CED\) are similar by the side-angle-side similarity criterion. Their corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac9{12}=\frac34.
\]
The two parts of \(AC\) therefore have ratio \(3:4\). Since \(AC=14\),
\[
AE=\frac{3}{3+4}\cdot14=\boxed6,
\]
choice \(\text{E}\).

Method 2: Use equal areas to find parallel sides

Adding the area of \(\triangle AEB\) to each of the given equal areas shows that \(\triangle ABD\) and \(\triangle ABC\) have equal areas. They share the positive base \(AB\), so their perpendicular heights from \(D\) and \(C\) to \(AB\) are equal.

Because \(ABCD\) is convex, \(C\) and \(D\) lie on the same side of \(AB\). Points at the same positive perpendicular distance on one side of a line lie on a parallel line. Hence \(CD\parallel AB\).

Now \(\angle AEB=\angle CED\) are vertical angles, and \(\angle ABE=\angle CDE\) are alternate interior angles formed by the parallel lines. Therefore \(\triangle AEB\) and \(\triangle CED\) are similar by angle-angle similarity. It follows that
\[
\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac9{12}=\frac34.
\]
Since \(E\) lies between \(A\) and \(C\), the length \(AC=14\) consists of \(3+4=7\) proportional parts. Thus
\[
AE=\frac37\cdot14=\boxed6,
\]
choice \(\text{E}\).
